text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as crude oil prices spiked sharply on escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, sending U.S. crude prices up noticeably and pushing Brent crude toward $110 a barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to stronger revenue and margins on every barrel they sell.

The two-week rally—up 15.6% since early October—reflects a broader tightening in global oil markets. Physical delivery costs have also surged (tanker rates are pushing the real cost of oil roughly $38 higher than the headline price), and geopolitical risks in a key shipping chokepoint have traders pricing in real supply concerns. This combination of higher prices and perceived scarcity is lifting the entire energy sector.
